How faithfully guest code is translated. Some games may only work at certain settings.
Reproduce the guarantees x86 makes about the order memory is written in. Off is much faster and highly likely to break a game that uses several threads.
Extend memory ordering to vector loads and stores. Stricter than most code needs, and noticeably slower.
Extend memory ordering to the repeated copy and fill instructions. Slower.
Repair an unaligned access with an instruction that keeps memory ordering, rather than a plain load or store. Off is faster and can tear a value another thread is writing.
Translate several blocks of guest code at once. Off is slower and makes it easier to say where a crash happened.
Emulate x87 floating point at 64-bit rather than 80-bit precision. Faster, and may cause rendering bugs.
Size the cache of translated blocks to what each thread is using. Off holds every thread\'s at the maximum, which costs around 150 MB.
Let the adaptive cache give memory back when a thread goes quiet. It strands translations made while the cache was larger, which stops the sound permanently and can freeze the picture.
Search a second, larger table before translating a block again. Costs memory and can avoid a stutter.
